chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Khallad, from Al-Sumaly, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'I do not love that I should humble myself for the sake of the red camels (great wealth), and there is no potion I have swallowed that is more beloved to me than the potion of anger, by which I do not requite its owner.'

key_terms.جُرْعَةِ غَيْظٍ: Potion of anger, metaphor for the experience of feeling anger
key_terms.حُمْرَ النَّعَمِ: Red camels, a metaphor for great wealth or bounties

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of suppressing anger according to Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) illustrates the supreme value of self-restraint by stating that swallowing the bitterness of anger without immediate retaliation is dearer to him than acquiring vast wealth, symbolized by 'red camels' (humr al-na'm), which represents significant material gain. This narration, found in Al-Kafi, emphasizes that preserving one's spiritual dignity and avoiding the loss of composure is superior to worldly accumulation, a key theme in Shia ethical teachings on character refinement (akhlaq).

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Khallad, from Al Sumaly,

(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not love it if I<sup>asws</sup> were to humiliate myself<sup>asws</sup> for the Bounties, and there is no potion from the potions to be swallowed, more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than the potion of anger, not seeking retribution by it from its agitator’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Khallad from al-Thumali from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following:

“I do not love to have the most noble of the bounties at the cost of humiliation to my soul. I have not swallowed any drop more beloved to me than the drop of anger for which I did not compensate from the one who caused it (my anger).”
